The constraint is not tools. The constraint is focus. The real enemy is not competition. It is distraction disguised as opportunity. Being a solo developer is not about doing everything. It is about owning everything.

And yet, solo development is one of the last places where leverage is still pure. One person with a laptop can design, build, deploy and monetise a system that reaches the world. That was science fiction not long ago.

You learn very quickly that velocity is not about typing speed. It is about decision speed. Most teams are slow because decisions are slow. As a solo developer you can move frighteningly fast, but you can also make catastrophic mistakes at the same speed.

Solo dev hits different. I built Drop the same way, just me shipping everything. Shows real-time foot traffic at restaurants and bars. Free on iOS.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/drop-realtime-foot-traffic/id6757093646

Being a solo developer is freedom and exposure at the same time. There is no stand-up to hide in. No product manager to deflect to. No architecture committee to argue with. If it breaks, it is you. If it ships, it is you.
